docs.title: Vacuum Manifolds
docs.text:
I use manifold here to describe a continuous enclosed volume that cannot be further segmented by valves. Pressure is not necessarily equal throughout a manifold due to conductance.

docs.title: Valves
docs.text:
All of the valves on the 2100F vacuum system are ultimately electronically controlled, with the exception of V5 which is manually actuated by rotating the sample holder to insert a sample into the column. Solenoid valves are directly controlled by an electrical signal, while pneumatic valves have one or more associated solenoids that switch air pressure to actuate the valve. The 3-way solenoid valves used in this system have two ports connected through the valve body at all times, while a third port connection is gated through the valve. The vacuum diagram is topologically simplified to only show the gated connections.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
The lower section of the microscope where the electron image is projected onto the phosphor screen and detectors (or in years past, Polaroid film). Connects upward to the column via V2 and to the high-vacuum DP manifold via V8. Can be roughed through RP2 or vented with N2 via V31.

docs.title: Column Pipe
docs.text:
The electron optical column + its interconnected vacuum standpipe. Bounded by the gun at the top (V1) and the camera chamber at the bottom (V2). Houses SIP1 (sputter ion pump). Also connects to the DP manifold via V10 and to the load-lock via V5.

docs.title: DP Manifold
docs.text:
The high-vacuum distribution manifold on the outlet side of the diffusion pump. Distributes DP pumping capacity to the main chambers (Camera via V8, Stage via V26, Column via V10) and connects to the RP2 roughing manifold via V27. Also has an N2 vent via V35.
